steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Depression symptoms: persistent low mood, loss of interest/pleasure (anhedonia), changes in sleep and appetite, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, feelings of worthlessness, and suicidal thoughts. Diagnosis requires symptoms lasting at least 2 weeks. | Key Fact: Biological explanations: genetics (twin studies show 37% concordance in MZ vs 15% in DZ twins - McGuffin et al.); neurotransmitter imbalance (low serotonin and noradrenaline); the diathesis-stress model: genetic predisposition + life events trigger depression. | Key Fact: Cognitive explanations: Beck's negative triad - negative views about the self, the world, and the future create a cycle of depression. Seligman's learned helplessness: repeated failure leads to belief that outcomes are uncontrollable, causing depression.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe biological and cognitive explanations of depression and evaluate each one. | Compare SSRI medication with CBT as treatments for depression. | Evaluate whether depression is best explained as a biological or a psychological condition.
